- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.3), model tends to overcorrect downward; reduce forecast dip depth or add slight upward bias.
- After strong upward spikes in history, model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast peak at 1.5–2x recent high or use moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment is positive and price is falling, model often underreacts — increase forecast slope slightly to match sentiment momentum.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive — add 0.5–1.0 to forecast for first 5–7 days if sentiment > 0.06.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating +/–), model overfits short-term noise — use 3–5 day moving average to filter out sentiment-driven jitter.
- If history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days falling), model often ignores it — adjust forecast to align with recent 5-day average if sentiment is weak or neutral.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate near-term (first 10 days) if sentiment is positive — reduce first 5–7 forecast values by 0.5–1.5 to match true trend.
